Drugs 2007; 67: 2747–79. Administration. Although rosiglitazone is licensed for use with other antidiabetic drugs the specifics of licensing and use may vary from country to country. In both the UK and USA, ros- iglitazone (Avandia; GSK) is licensed for use with metformin or a sulfonylurea, or both if necessary, in patients in whom single or dual agent therapy is inadequate. In the UK, however, NICE rec- ommends dual therapy only in patients who cannot be given combination therapy with metformin plus a sulfonylurea.1 The combination of rosiglitazone with insulin is now generally avoided because of an increased risk of heart failure and other cardiac adverse events (see also Effects on the Heart, above), al- though licensed product information may not necessarily contra- indicate the combination. In the UK, licensed product informa- tion for rosiglitazone warns that insulin should only be added to established rosiglitazone therapy in exceptional cases and under close supervision.
